tob-10806: First published in 1948, A. W. Tozer’s slim devotional classic urges Christians to seek God not as an idea but as a living presence. His ten short chapters — on faith, stillness, and the stripping away of self — are written with prophetic urgency. The book has sold millions and remains one of the most loved works of modern evangelical spirituality.
tob-13506: Saint Augustine wrote The City of God after Rome was sacked in 410, answering pagans who blamed the disaster on Christianity. This second volume continues his grand argument contrasting the earthly city, built on love of self, with the heavenly city, built on love of God. It is one of the founding works of Western political thought.
tob-4006: Benvenuto Cellini — goldsmith, sculptor, brawler — wrote the most swaggering life-story of the Renaissance. He brags of his art, his duels, his jailbreaks, and his run-ins with popes and kings, all in a voice of wild self-belief. The book is a front-row seat to sixteenth-century Italy at its most colorful.
tob-10808-50206: The second volume of von Hügel’s study turns to the thought-side of mysticism — how inner knowing stands toward reason, churches, and the wider life of belief. He takes the mystics’ part against scoffers and hotheads alike. The two volumes together form one of the deepest modern probings of the theme.
tob-4206: W. Warde Fowler’s famed lectures rebuild what faith felt like to common Romans — their house-gods, feast-days, and fussy care for doing rites right. He tracks how this workaday worship yielded to eastern cults and Christ. The book is the kindliest door into Roman religion.
tob-4306: M. Friedländer’s Englishing of Maimonides’ Guide leads the puzzled reader between faith and reason — showing how the Bible’s hard sayings open to right thinking. The medieval master’s masterwork, it fathered Jewish rationalism. This version long served as the English standard.
tob-0006: The Tanakh — the Hebrew Bible — strings Torah, Prophets, and Writings: the ground-books of Judaism and Christianity’s Old Testament. From Genesis to Chronicles its books bent western law, letters, and worship. This entry gives the whole Hebrew canon.
tob-4106: Arthur Gilchrist Brodeur’s rendering of Snorri’s Prose Edda is the classic English of the Norse tale-handbook. His notes steer readers through gods and etins, the world’s making and its unmaking at Ragnarok. Myth-learners and bookmen have leaned on it for a hundred years. The volume keeps the old tales alive and clear.
cia-0000108006: The fifth report to the president from his Board of Consultants on Foreign Intelligence, dated February 1960. Outside experts reviewed the spy agencies and told Eisenhower what was working and what was not. The document is oversight history — the presidency trying to keep its secret servants honest and effective.
cia-0000119206: A November 1968 companion report on American, Thai, and Philippine prisoners held in Laos — locations of four camps, the truncated title suggests. Filed two days after its sibling report, it shows the steady accumulation of POW intelligence. Each report added a few more pins to the map of the missing.
cia-0000119706: A February 1953 estimate of probable developments in Egypt. The revolution of 1952 had toppled the king, and Nasser was consolidating power. The document watches a new strongman rise — the man who would nationalize Suez and defy the West.
cia-0000124306: A November 1950 report on American POWs at Mukden and Erhmienpa — Manchurian cities deep in China's northeast. Early in the Korean War, prisoners were already being moved into China proper. The document is an early sighting in what would become a vast, tragic geography.
cia-0000132306: Situation Report 616: Jordan denying it violated the UN arms embargo — the truncated title suggests more. Amman walked a tightrope between Arab solidarity and Western pressure. The document is the denial, filed: a kingdom's balancing act, on record.
cia-0000132606: Item 1 in the July 1960 general series: Yugoslav-Cuban relations. Tito's maverick communism and Castro's revolution found common ground. The document is the heretics, meeting: the independents, comparing notes.
cia-0000135806: A 1954 cable to a senior representative — name deleted — requesting guidance. The field asked headquarters what to do. The document is the question: the operatives, awaiting orders.
cia-0000136006: A 1954 routing sheet with a LINCOLN cable on courier and pouch information. The mail had to move securely. The entry is the channel: the couriers, listed — the pouches, tracked.
cia-0000136206: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on the availability of F-47 fighter planes, critical to the operation. The invasion needed air power. The document is the aircraft: the fighters, counted — the operation, depending on them.
un-ga-res-106: General Assembly Resolution 106, cataloged with the year 1915 — three decades before the UN existed, an impossible date. The designation is preserved; the year is plainly wrong. The entry is the error: the number, kept — the date, impossible.
un-sc-res-106: Security Council Resolution 106, cataloged with the year 1948 — the numbering suggests the mid-1950s, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1406: Security Council Resolution 1406, adopted in 2002 — aligned. The new century's Council at work. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-1506: Security Council Resolution 1506, cataloged with the year 1999 — the numbering suggests 2003, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-1606: Security Council Resolution 1606, cataloged with the year 2002 — the numbering suggests 2005, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-1706: Security Council Resolution 1706, cataloged with the year 1990 — though the well-known Darfur force resolution of that number belongs to 2006, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted — and the subject is left to the text.
un-sc-res-1806: Security Council Resolution 1806, adopted in 2008 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
cia-0000132506: A 1961 CIA file on Cuba, numbered 0000132506. The archive's bare title hides the contents. The entry is the placeholder: the subject, Cuba — the details, in the file.
cia-0000136706: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136706. The invasion year's firm-dated archive. The document is the archive: the year, fateful.
plos-pone-0000006: A 2006 PLOS ONE study establishing clonal cell lines with endothelial-like potential from CD-something cells — the truncated title cuts off the source. The team grew uniform cell lines that can act like blood-vessel lining. The paper is the method: the cells, cloned — the potential, endothelial.
cia-0000136306: A 1954 CIA cable from Lincoln — the Guatemala coup station — for Cadick and Broadfrost, an order on a strike mission, the truncated title suggests. The PBSUCCESS operation's air war, directed by cable. The document is the order: the strike, commanded.
moyle-institutes-justinian-1906: J. B. Moyle's 1906 translation of the Institutes of Justinian — the sixth-century Roman law textbook that taught emperors' law to students for a thousand years and still underlies civil-law systems. Rome's legal mind, in English. The book is the textbook: the law, Roman.
wieger-textes-philosophiques-1906: Léon Wieger's 1906 Textes philosophiques — the Jesuit sinologist's collection of Chinese philosophical texts, opening classical Chinese thought to French readers. Confucians, Taoists, and Buddhists, in translation. The book is the bridge: the Chinese classics, crossed over.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d106: Generalissimo Chiang to President Roosevelt, November 9, 1943 — Document 106. China's leader replied. The message is the reply: Chiang, writing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d206: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, November 10, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 206. London answered the same day. The message is the quickness: the reply, immediate.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d306: An American draft of the communiqué with amendments by President Roosevelt — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 306. The announcement, in draft, marked by the president's hand. The draft is the announcement: the words, Roosevelt's.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d406: The president's special assistant Hopkins to the president, and the — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 406. The insider wrote widely. The memo is the insider's: Hopkins, informing.
the-spirit-of-1906: George Brooks captures the mood of a remarkable year — 1906 — when San Francisco's earthquake, political upheavals, and new inventions made the world feel both fragile and thrilling. His reflections take stock of a nation testing itself. A vivid time capsule of American optimism and anxiety at the dawn of the modern age.
arxiv-2605-08906: Sound waves can push tiny particles around inside microfluidic chips, sorting cells and droplets. T. Sujith and A. K. Sen show that making the fluid viscoelastic — springy as well as syrupy — gives finer control over that acoustic migration and trapping. The 2026 paper is microfluidics for lab-on-a-chip devices.
arxiv-2605-09106: Money decisions attract human biases — overconfidence, loss aversion — and LLMs trained on human text inherit them. Xiaoyu Hu and Jinman Zhao introduce Fin-Bias, a comprehensive evaluation of LLM decision-making under human bias in finance. The 2026 paper stress-tests AI bankers for all-too-human flaws.
arxiv-2605-09006: An induced diamond — two triangles sharing an edge, with no extra connections — is a pattern networks may hide. Keren Censor-Hillel, Tomer Even, and Virginia Vassilevska Williams study witness-sensitive detection of these diamonds in distributed settings. The 2026 paper is graph algorithms with an eye on who sees what.
arxiv-2605-09506: Reconstructing evolutionary trees the Bayesian way is brutally slow — every candidate tree demands expensive likelihood computations. Wentao Yu and Shijia Wang accelerate the inference with delayed acceptance sequential Monte Carlo using random forest surrogates. The 2026 paper makes phylogenetics dramatically faster.
arxiv-2605-09606: Image-to-3D models sometimes generate harmful geometry — broken, dangerous, or disallowed shapes. Yule Liu, Yilong Yang, Jiale Teng, and colleagues study both the generation and the mitigation of the problem. The 2026 paper is safety research for 3D generative AI.
arxiv-2605-09806: Reasoning traces waste tokens on easy steps; adaptive length saves them for the hard ones. Songtao Wei, Zhikai Li, Yuede Ji, and colleagues make reasoning length-efficient, adaptive, and dynamic — LEAD. The 2026 paper is efficient thinking for large language models.
arxiv-2605-09906: Audio-visual LLMs suffer cross-modal interference — sound corrupting sight and vice versa; separating first and fusing later mitigates it. Xuanchen Li, Yuheng Lu, Chenrui Cui, and colleagues propose the strategy. The 2026 paper is multimodal reasoning without the harmful crosstalk.
arxiv-2605-10106: Spatial reasoning over video for multimodal large language models — ViSRA is the agent. Tingshu Mou, Jiabo He, Renying Wang, and colleagues build it. The 2026 paper is spatial AI for video understanding. It reasons carefully about space in moving images.
plos-pone-0003406: Stem-cell biologists hunted an ancient instruction program in this 2008 paper. Comparing which genes turn on together during embryonic stem-cell differentiation across species, they found co-expression patterns conserved through evolution. Those shared programs point to core rules for how stem cells choose their fate, knowledge that could steady lab-grown tissues and therapies.
plos-pone-0003506: Diabetes researchers tied a stress kinase to insulin in this 2008 multi-population study. Variation in the SGK1 gene tracked with differences in insulin secretion across European groups, and the team confirmed the pattern through the TUEF cohort. The result nominates SGK1 as a candidate gene for type 2 diabetes, linking a salt-handling enzyme to blood-sugar control.
plos-pone-0003606: Behavioral neuroscientists Auger and Forbes-Lorman found a hormone receptor calming male rats in this 2008 study. Progesterone's anxiety-reducing effects were traced specifically through the progestin receptor, not just general hormone action. The result clarifies the molecular route by which a reproductive hormone steadies the anxious brain.
plos-pone-0003706: In 2008, Langer, Malykhin, and Maeda fingered an anthrax wall piece as an alarm trigger. Peptidoglycan from Bacillus anthracis drove human monocytes to launch an inflammatory response through the p38 pathway. The finding names a bacterial building block behind the deadly inflammation of inhaled anthrax.
plos-pone-0003806: Bain, Singkran, and Mills weighed a lake's competing needs in this 2008 paper. Their integrated ecosystem assessment tackled Lake Ontario water management, balancing public interests with ecological dynamics. The framework shows how to run a great lake for people and nature together.
plos-pone-0003906: A 2008 genetics methods paper sorted two kinds of variation at once. Lee, Kasif, and Weng analyzed single-letter changes sitting inside copy-number-variable regions. The joint analysis stops one kind of variation from masquerading as the other.
plos-pone-0004006: In 2008, Gigandet, Hagmann, and Kurant graded the reliability of brain wiring maps. They estimated confidence levels for white-matter connections drawn from MRI tractography. Not every reconstructed fiber deserves equal trust, their careful analysis clearly showed. The confidence framework helps brain imagers separate real tracts from imaging artifacts.
plos-pone-0004106: In 2008, a Chinese team found a fertility gatekeeper in rats. The epididymis protein HongrES1 tightly controlled sperm capacitation in rats. Without it, sperm failed to ready themselves for egg fusion. The protein marks a new target for future male contraception.
plos-pone-0004206: In 2009, Mangano, Clark, and Auburn cleared a suspect malaria gene. Interferon regulatory factor 1 showed no link to severe malaria in tested trios. The immune transcription factor fully dodged blame. The clean negative result redirects the malaria-gene hunt elsewhere fast.
plos-pone-0004306: In 2009, Nikolaev, Zheng, and Wardill mapped how fly eyes adjust fast. Retinal network adaptation improved temporal coding of natural scenes greatly. The second paper pinned down the true mechanisms. The neat work shows fly eyes tuning themselves to the world.
plos-pone-0357206: Heart failure monitoring usually means blood draws — but saliva might do. This paper compared salivary and serum levels of NT-proBNP, troponin, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein in heart failure patients. The saliva-blood comparison tests whether a spit test could track failing hearts.
plos-pone-0357406: Railway logistics yards live or die on crane scheduling. This paper optimized multi-objective flexible scheduling for container rail-mounted gantry cranes. The scheduling model balances competing goals — speed, energy use, fairness across jobs — keeping the whole yard humming instead of jammed.
plos-pone-0357806: Who drives rehabilitation science in Canada? This observational study measured research productivity and impact of rehabilitation science faculty across the country, using publicly available and survey data. The faculty-wide picture shows where the field is strong, where it is thin, and who is shaping its future.
plos-pone-0356006: African swine fever virus threatens the world’s pork supply — and researchers need fast genomic tools. PePApipe is a complete bioinformatics analysis pipeline purpose-built for the African swine fever virus genome. The pipeline gives scientists a one-stop toolkit for tracking and understanding this devastating pathogen.
plos-pone-0357906: Stressed physicians desperately need relief — they can’t pour from an empty cup. Project FIERCE is a randomized controlled trial protocol testing a positive emotion-focused meditation intervention for physicians with elevated stress. The planned trial will test whether meditation can genuinely heal the healers.
plos-pone-0357706: The triglyceride-glucose index — a simple metabolic marker — may predict death in fibrotic lung disease. This retrospective study linked the index to all-cause mortality in non-diabetic patients with fibrotic lung disease receiving antifibrotic therapy. The marker could refine prognosis with a routine blood test.
plos-pone-0356906: Idarubicin — a mainstay against blood cancers — must stay stable from pharmacy to patient. This one-month physicochemical stability study tested the drug prepared in polyolefin-type infusion bags. The stability data give hospital pharmacies the confidence to prepare doses safely in advance.
plos-pone-0355606: Cervical cancers resist immunotherapy through epigenetic trickery involving HDAC2. This paper showed HDAC2 restrains IGF2BP1-associated m6A dysregulation driving that resistance. The mechanistic chain reveals a druggable target that could re-sensitize tumors to immune attack.
plos-pone-0357006: Rickettsioses — tick- and mite-borne fevers — plague Sri Lanka in shifting patterns. This 2009–2023 spatio-temporal analysis with climate-linked modeling tracked their seasonal and spatial trends. The maps and models guide control efforts as the climate shifts the diseases’ range.
plos-pone-0356806: How you grow dendritic cells in the dish changes what they become. This paper mapped the phenotypic and functional patterns of murine bone marrow-derived dendritic cells under different in vitro differentiation conditions. The patterns give immunologists a practical guide to generating the cells they actually want.
plos-pone-0356206: Aging eyes can be trained like aging muscles — perhaps. This pilot randomized trial tested the effect of vision training on visual function in older adults. The preliminary results suggest structured visual exercise might genuinely sharpen seniors’ sight, opening a non-surgical path to better vision.
plos-pone-0343606: Detecting E. coli in drinking water quickly can prevent outbreaks. This paper applied machine learning to detect the bacterium in Bangladeshi drinking water. The ML-powered detection promises faster, cheaper water safety monitoring where laboratory infrastructure is thin.
plos-pone-0342806: Undergraduates can do real genetics — studying how structural variants affect gene expression in C. elegans balancers. This paper described a course-based undergraduate research experience (CURE) built around that question. The CURE model brings authentic discovery into the teaching lab.
plos-pone-0355106: A fungus that kills malaria mosquitoes — Metarhizium pingshaense — affects more than the infected generation. This paper studied maternal and cross-stage effects of fungal infection on Anopheles coluzzii life history. The findings reveal how the biopesticide’s damage echoes across mosquito generations.
plos-pone-0352906: Brain sigma-1 receptors — implicated in neurodegeneration and pain — need better imaging ligands. This paper developed bis-hydrophobic budding leads targeting these receptors. The novel ligands promise sharper PET imaging of a receptor at the frontier of neuroscience drug discovery.
plos-pone-0354606: Nigerian frontline healthcare workers faced COVID-19 with remarkable serological footprints. This paper found high SARS-CoV-2 antibody prevalence among them across three states from August to December 2022. The seroprevalence data reveal the pandemic’s true reach among those who faced it first.
plos-pone-0353606: Absorbing microwaves efficiently in a thin layer is key to stealth and EMI shielding. This paper designed a single-layer six-band metasurface absorber for microwave applications. The multi-band absorber soaks up radiation across six frequency bands — a compact solution to electromagnetic pollution.
plos-pone-0354706: Knowing a lithium-ion battery’s true health — beyond what the charge gauge says — prevents failures. This paper predicted battery state of health via a back propagation network using multi-feature combinations of electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. The AI approach reads the battery’s electrical fingerprints to forecast its remaining useful life with impressive accuracy.
plos-pone-0355506: Tanzanian patients with mechanical heart valves take warfarin for life — with daily challenges. This qualitative study explored their day-to-day experiences at a national cardiac institute. The patients’ accounts reveal the dietary restrictions, bleeding fears, and monitoring burdens that define life on anticoagulation.
plos-pone-0355406: Quinoa in Bangladesh — a promising new crop — faces a newly reported enemy. This paper is the first report of Curvularia alcornii causing leaf spot of quinoa in the country. The finding alerts growers and pathologists to a threat that could nip a nutritious crop in the bud.
europmc-pmc2868906: Gene switches that stay on, and one that answers to a drug, each have their place. This 2010 paper compares constitutive promoters with the doxycycline-inducible promoter head to head. The authors' bake-off guides vector design. Their data helps biologists pick the right switch.
europmc-pmc2874506: Clear reporting makes research useful, and this 2010 paper preaches the creed. The authors argue transparent and accurate reporting boosts reliability, utility, and impact, spotlighting guidelines and the EQUATOR Network. Their call rallied journals. The paper helped make reporting checklists the norm.
europmc-pmc2874806: Cells run vast chemical webs, and this 2010 paper offers the atlas. The authors present BiGG, a knowledgebase of large-scale metabolic reconstructions for many species. Their curated maps let researchers simulate cell chemistry on computers. The resource became a standard toolkit for systems biology labs.
europmc-pmc2918506: Light weights with many reps may build muscle best. This 2010 study finds low-load high-volume resistance exercise stimulates muscle protein synthesis more than heavy low-volume work in young men. The authors overturn gym lore. Their result reshaped training advice.
europmc-pmc2929606: A tagged histone flags DNA breaks, and this 2010 review follows the signal. The authors cover the H2AX tag's role in DNA damage response and cancer therapy. Their overview shows a marker turned drug target. The review connects basic cell biology to treatment.
europmc-pmc3012106: Old age brings disease clusters, not single ills. This 2010 paper maps which chronic ills travel together in the elderly. The authors reveal the tangled webs. Their work guides elder care. Heart, lung, and mood ills often team up. Doctors now treat the cluster, not just one.
europmc-pmc3019106: Chagas tests needed standardizing. This 2011 world study compares DNA tests for the Chagas parasite in patients' blood. The authors' bake-off guides labs. Their work aids diagnosis. Millions carry the silent parasite. Better tests catch it before heart damage. Blood banks screen donors with these tests.
europmc-pmc3029306: Colon cancer patients carry jumbled gut germs. This 2011 paper finds the gut germ mix off-balance in bowel cancer patients. The authors reveal the skew. Their work points to stool-test markers. Bad actors bloom while guardians fade. Stool tests may spot risk years early.
europmc-pmc3091306: Fat chemistry got a query language. This 2011 paper brings a search language for high-speed lipid fingerprinting. The authors' concept sped fat ID. Their work aids metabolism studies. Thousands of fats get named per run. Clinics hunt disease markers in the data.
europmc-pmc6506906: Osteosarcoma is a bone cancer that strikes mostly children and teenagers. This paper reports survival results for more than 2,000 patients treated through EURAMOS-1, a joint European and American research effort. By pooling so many cases of a rare disease, the study gives doctors their clearest picture yet of who survives, who relapses, and what drives the odds.
europmc-pmc6510306: Farm animals receive huge amounts of antibiotics, a practice that fuels drug-resistant germs threatening human health. This paper makes the case for cutting that use and maps out how it can be done. It reviews strategies from policy changes to better farming practices, showing how the world could keep livestock healthy while slowing the rise of superbugs.
europmc-pmc6523806: When water runs short, plants fight back with chemistry: antioxidant systems that mop up the destructive molecules drought unleashes inside cells. This review details the plant antioxidant network and how it helps crops survive dry spells and recover afterward. Breeding or engineering stronger antioxidant defenses could protect harvests as droughts grow more frequent.
europmc-pmc6524306: Bacteria living in biofilms - slimy surface communities - can survive antibiotic doses that would kill them floating free. This review surveys the battleground: how the biofilm matrix blocks drugs, how embedded cells enter dormant states, and how communities share resistance. Understanding these defenses is essential for treating the chronic infections biofilms cause.
europmc-pmc6542806: Dig into soil anywhere on Earth and the fungi you find are surprisingly familiar. Surveying 235 soils worldwide, researchers found just a few Ascomycota groups dominating fungal communities across continents. The study maps which fungi rule the underground and what climates and soils they prefer - a first global census of Earth's hidden fungal majority.
europmc-pmc6562906: Stem cells may heal mainly through what they spill: the secretome - a broth of proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, and tiny vesicles that cells release. This review gathers evidence that this cell-free cocktail rivals whole stem-cell transplants in therapeutic effect. Bottling the secretome could deliver the benefits of cell therapy without the cells.
europmc-pmc6667406: Probiotics only help if they stick around - adhesion to the gut wall is step one. This review examines how probiotic and prebiotic compounds grip intestinal surfaces and what that means for health: better colonization, stronger barriers, tuned immunity. Sticky microbes, it turns out, are useful microbes.
europmc-pmc6756106: Psychiatry lacks the growth charts pediatrics enjoys - until now. This paper frames mental disorders as deviations from normative brain functioning, using statistical models of typical variation. The normative approach spots where an individual veers off course, personalizing diagnosis.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-106: A hard-hitting 2007 Government Accountability Office report on FEMA's handling of housing maintenance contracts in Mississippi after Hurricane Katrina. Investigators found weak oversight that allowed millions of dollars in waste and potential fraud — paying for work that was never done or done badly. The report traces how contracts were awarded and monitored, and recommends tighter controls for future disaster recovery spending.
gao-gaoreports-b-299906: A Government Accountability Office bid-protest decision dated September 25, 2007, filed by Bighorn Lumber Company, Inc. The lumber firm challenged a federal timber or wood-products contract award, and the ruling applies procurement law to its claims. The published decision records GAO's reasoning for companies competing in the federal timber market.
gao-gaoreports-b-299806: AHNTECH cried foul over an August 2007 award, and GAO's ruling is the last word. The tech firm said the agency's pick was unfair; the call tests the protest against bid law. For small tech shops, each published ruling is a free lesson in how the federal buying game is really played.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1006: The new passports were tougher to fake in 2007 — but GAO's report says the fraud fight was not won. Chips and security inks helped, yet gaps remained for forgers to exploit. The findings balance credit for the upgrade against the forger's eternal ingenuity.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-206: The immigration lawyers were drowning in cases in 2007 — GAO's report says the workload review and staffing plans lacked data and proof. The findings demand real numbers before real hiring. The report's logic is simple: you cannot staff a flood you refuse to measure.
openalex-w7207808606: Emergency rooms use triage systems to decide who gets seen first, and the Manchester Protocol is one of the most common. This paper studies how that system performs with elderly patients, whose symptoms can be harder to read and whose numbers are growing fast. The authors weigh its effectiveness and the challenges staff face applying it to older adults. The goal is safer, fairer sorting of urgent cases in an aging population.
openalex-w7204997306: Rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms appear, and in rural Brazil it still circulates among wild animals. This study surveyed residents of Cha Grande, Pernambuco, about their perceptions of rabies and how they interact with domestic animals and wildlife. The authors map the knowledge gaps that keep the disease a threat. A grounded piece of public-health research where human behavior and animal ecology meet.
openalex-w4410112906: Lung infections need antibiotics that reach the airways. This study measured lascufloxacin levels in lung lining fluid, finding concentrations far above blood levels. The authors tested the drug's promise for respiratory infections. A pharmacology study of an antibiotic that goes where it is needed.
pmc-13469906: A 2026 paper on measuring mental effort without invasive sensors, aimed at training and high-stakes jobs. The authors review signal-processing techniques and the evidence behind using body signals — like heart rate patterns — to estimate cognitive load. Reliable measurement could help design safer training for pilots, surgeons, and operators.
pmc-13472206: A 2026 correspondence piece responding to a life-cycle assessment comparing marine scrubbers — exhaust-cleaning systems on ships — with low-sulfur fuels, measured from well to wake. Letters like this are part of science's open debate, raising questions or corrections about published findings. It reflects the ongoing argument over the cleanest way to power shipping.
pmc-13447906: This 2026 radiotherapy paper reports a prospective trial testing whether HyperSight CBCT — a newer cone-beam CT scanner — calculates radiation dose accurately enough for adaptive head-and-neck treatment. Adaptive therapy re-plans as anatomy changes, and it lives or dies on dose accuracy. The trial gives clinicians the numbers they need.
pmc-13385206: In this 2026 cell biology paper, researchers uncovered caspase-mediated cleavage events that are hidden by secondary proteolysis during apoptosis — programmed cell death. The cell's demolition is messier than the textbook picture, with cuts obscured by further cutting. The finding refines the map of how cells die.
pmc-13322706: This 2026 Australian study tested the feasibility of a no-ultrasound screening tool for early medical abortion — assessing eligibility without a scan. Removing the ultrasound requirement could widen access, especially in rural areas. The feasibility study is the first step toward changing practice.
pmc-13464506: In this 2026 plant pathology paper, researchers built a genome-scale metabolic model of a plant-bacterium pathosystem to illuminate bacterial wilt — a devastating crop disease. Modeling the full metabolism of host and pathogen reveals the battle's weak points. The model is a new tool for fighting wilt.
pmc-13449906: This 2026 retrospective case series covered imaging findings and diagnostic challenges of intravenous leiomyomatosis — a benign smooth-muscle tumor that grows through veins. The wandering tumor confounds diagnosis. The series is the reference.
pmc-13558506: This 2026 prospective multinational observational cohort study (AD-REAL) examined clinical effectiveness and treatment discontinuation of oral systemics for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (the title is truncated). Real-world dermatology data guide prescribing. The cohort is the evidence.
pmc-13530706: A 2026 conference poster finding blood flow restriction therapy after ACL reconstruction did not improve strength or thigh muscle volume at 12 weeks. The trendy rehab adjunct disappointed. The poster reports the negative result.
pmc-13448306: A 2026 conference abstract (TLSB-07) on clinical and pathological variables associated with brain metastasis development among patients receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The abstract reports early findings. Conference abstracts preserve the presented work.
pmc-13509006: This 2026 computational paper, "Bend and Snap," explored helix bias computationally to classify Abl kinase allosteric modulators. The kinase's shape predicted drug type. The classifier is the tool.
pmc-13498906: This 2026 paper expanded the PETase landscape through structure-guided extremophile genome mining — revealing PET-hydrolyzing true lipase lineages. The plastic-eating enzymes multiplied. The mining is the method.
pmc-13537106: In this 2026 HIV paper, circulating platelet-natural killer cell complexes were elevated in people living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy. The cell complexes marked the treated infection. The elevation is the biomarker.
pmc-13489206: This 2026 paper showed LPA1-induced epithelial-mesenchymal transition of retinal pigment epithelial cells promoted subretinal fibrosis via USP1-mediated deubiquitination and stabilization of ZEB1. The eye's scarring pathway was mapped. The mechanism is the target.
pmc-13452006: This 2026 umbrella review comprehensively examined dance-based interventions for mental health — definitions, measurement practices, and evidence quality (the title is truncated). The dance therapy evidence was graded. The review is the synthesis.
pmc-13444706: This 2026 correction notice amended a European network overview on optimizing treatment with therapeutic antibodies in chronic inflammatory diseases (the title is truncated). Corrections fix the record. This entry preserves the correction.
pmc-13438106: In this 2026 medicinal chemistry paper, substituted dihydropyrimidinones were rationally designed, synthesized, and biologically evaluated as antibacterial agents and beta-lactamase inhibitors (the title is truncated). The dual-action compounds were optimized. The evaluation is the pipeline.
pmc-13428706: A 2026 in silico paper identifying selective cyclodecapeptide inhibitors targeting the Plasmodium falciparum Grp78 chaperone. The malaria chaperone's inhibitors were computationally found. The identification is the lead generation.
pmc-13420306: In this 2026 mouse study, high-fat diet and treadmill running effects on bone marrow fat and bone properties in young males were tested. The diet-exercise-bone triangle was mapped. The effects are the finding.
pmc-13416006: A 2026 population-based cohort study of outcomes for women with diabetes at late preterm gestation who received antenatal corticosteroids. The steroids' maternal-fetal effects were tracked. The outcomes inform obstetrics.
pmc-13453306: A 2026 surgical cohort study on spread through air spaces in multiple synchronous bilateral primary lung cancer — prognostic implications. The STAS phenomenon's prognosis was quantified. The implications guide surgery.
